title: Read image EXIF, IPTC, and XMP metadata
objective: When Lap indexes an image or RAW file, read descriptive and capture metadata that already exists in the file and in a sibling XMP sidecar, store the file-owned values in the local catalog, and show and search them without writing anything back to the photo or the sidecar.
context: Lap 0.3.2 already reads embedded EXIF while indexing images and RAW files. kamadak-exif is the primary reader, little_exif fills missing JPEG capture settings, LibRaw fills missing RAW fields, and a binary TIFF-tag scrape is the last resort. Video metadata is read separately in t_video.rs.
IPTC IIM and XMP are not read. The only XMP use today is locating an embedded motion-photo video in t_motion_photo.rs.

Scan skips .xmp and .aae files in is_ignored_scan_sidecar in src-tauri/src/t_utils.rs, so sidecars are not library items. Apple AAE sidecars are copied, renamed, and deleted with their photos, but their contents are not metadata.

Catalog rows in afiles already store camera, lens, exposure, artist, copyright, description, orientation, and GPS. Lap rating, favorites, comments, culling, tags, and collections are library data. AFile::update writes rating from the struct, and update_file_info copies the previous rating back first. Comments, favorites, and culling are not rewritten by that update.
Filename search matches afiles.name and afiles.comments only. The file info panel in src-vite/src/components/FileInfo.vue renders the existing EXIF fields. Editable stars bind to fileInfo.rating.
The latest schema migration is version 17. AFile selects and from_row use positional column indexes, including a second copy of that select in src-tauri/src/t_dedup.rs.

Unchanged files are not re-read: add_to_db_with_raw_info refreshes metadata only when the image mtime changes, the thumbnail is missing, or a one-time motion-photo or TIFF check applies. A sidecar-only change does not change the image mtime.
constraints: Reading metadata must not modify image bytes, XMP sidecars, or AAE sidecars.
Do not copy file keywords, XMP labels, or XMP ratings into Lap tags, comments, favorites, culling_flag, or afiles.rating.
Do not take orientation, pixel dimensions, or media subtype from IPTC, XMP, or a sidecar.
Keep kamadak-exif, little_exif, and LibRaw as the primary capture-metadata readers. IPTC and XMP only fill capture fields that those readers left empty.
A malformed packet, a truncated sidecar, or an unsupported container must not fail indexing of that file.
Sidecar paths must be siblings of the image. Do not follow paths or URLs stored inside XMP.
Do not log titles, keywords, GPS coordinates, or other metadata values.
Create and stay on feature/read-image-metadata for integration. Child work merges back into that branch, not into main.
out_of_scope: Writing or updating EXIF, IPTC, or XMP in images or sidecars, including changes to the editor metadata-copy path except where needed so it still does not emit IPTC or XMP.
Importing embedded keywords, labels, or ratings into Lap tags, comments, favorites, culling, or the editable rating.
Applying Lightroom, darktable, DxO, Capture One, or Apple AAE develop adjustments.
Reading non-XMP sidecars such as .aae, .dop, .pp3, .cos, .cot, or .on1.
Indexing .xmp or .aae files as photos or videos.
Replacing the existing video metadata reader.
Changing orientation, thumbnail generation, embeddings, face detection, or duplicate hashing as part of a metadata refresh.
success_criteria: A newly indexed JPEG, PNG or TIFF, and RAW file exposes embedded IPTC and XMP title, description, keywords, creator, copyright, and capture fields that the current EXIF readers did not already fill.
A sibling XMP sidecar overrides embedded descriptive metadata using the plan precedence, and an image-only EXIF file keeps today's indexed values.

Changing, replacing, or removing a sidecar updates the catalog on the next scan without rewriting the sidecar, deleting the thumbnail, clearing embeddings, or changing Lap rating, favorites, comments, tags, or culling.
The file info panel shows the new descriptive values, library text search matches them, and README states that this metadata is read and still not written.
notes: Detail level is high because the request asked for detailed issues.
The primary checkout should be created from main as feature/read-image-metadata before parallel workers start. Parallel issue branches fork from that branch and merge back into it.

title: Parse embedded and sidecar image metadata
description: Add a read-only metadata model and parsers for IPTC IIM, XMP, image-container packets, and sibling XMP sidecars. Existing EXIF readers stay in place. This epic produces tested parse results and does not change the catalog or the UI.
acceptance_criteria: A single in-memory metadata value can represent descriptive fields and capture gap-fill fields from IPTC, XMP, and sidecars.
IPTC, XMP, container extraction, and sidecar discovery each have fixture tests that do not require a Lap library database.
Orientation and Lap-owned library fields are absent from the parsed model.

title: Store read metadata and follow sidecars
description: Persist the file-owned metadata on afiles, fill it while indexing, refresh it when a sidecar changes, and move the sibling XMP file with Lap file operations. Library-owned columns stay under their current controls.
acceptance_criteria: New and refreshed catalog rows store supplemental metadata without overwriting Lap rating, favorites, comments, tags, or culling.
Existing libraries gain the columns idempotently and backfill on the next scan without thumbnail or embedding regeneration.
Rename, move, copy, import, and delete keep the bound XMP sidecar with the image and do not treat AAE files as XMP.

title: Show, search, and document read metadata
description: Present the newly stored descriptive metadata in the file info panel, include it in library text search, and update the user-facing metadata explanation so it matches read-only behavior.
acceptance_criteria: File info shows title, headline, keywords, credit, label, embedded rating, and recorded place when those values exist, and the editable Lap rating control still uses afiles.rating.
Library text search matches the new descriptive text and the existing name and comment fields.
English and translated READMEs say Lap reads embedded IPTC, embedded XMP, and XMP sidecars and still does not write library data into them.

title: Define the read-only metadata model and merge rules
description: Create the shared Rust model that later parsers and the indexer will fill. Lap already stores EXIF capture fields on AFile. This task adds the in-memory value used for IPTC, XMP, and sidecar data, plus pure merge functions. It does not read files and does not change SQLite.
acceptance_criteria: FileMetadata can hold title, headline, description, keywords, creator, copyright, credit, city, state, country, label, embedded rating, capture date, camera and lens names, exposure fields, and GPS, and it has no orientation, width, height, rating, favorite, comment, tag, or culling field.

Scalar descriptive fields use the first non-empty value in caller-supplied precedence order. Keywords are trimmed, control characters are removed, duplicates are dropped case-sensitively, earlier layers come first, and the result is capped at 64 keywords of 128 characters.
Embedded rating accepts only integers 0 through 5. Missing, negative, and out-of-range ratings stay empty. Empty strings do not override a lower-precedence value.
Capture gap-fill copies make, model, lens, exposure, ISO, flash, software, capture date, and GPS only into fields that are currently empty. It never writes orientation or dimensions.
The module is registered from main.rs and exposes a stub read_supplemental_metadata that returns an empty value until the indexing task implements it.
constraints: Do not add XML or image crates in this task.
Do not change AFile, migrations, or the frontend.
Stub submodule files must compile. Parser tasks own the real implementations.
implementation_notes: Put the public types and merge functions in t_file_metadata/mod.rs. Declare the four submodules there so later tasks can edit their own files without editing main.rs again.
Map embedded rating separately from Lap rating. Lightroom uses -1 for a reject flag; leave that unmapped rather than turning it into culling.
Normalize keywords by trimming Unicode whitespace and dropping values that are empty after cleanup. Preserve original case.
Provide fill_capture_gaps(&mut destination, &source) and merge_layers(layers) where the slice is highest precedence first.
read_supplemental_metadata(path) -> FileMetadata returns FileMetadata::default() for now. Indexing will replace the body.
implementation_steps: Add mod t_file_metadata; to src-tauri/src/main.rs next to the other t_* modules.
Create src-tauri/src/t_file_metadata/mod.rs with FileMetadata, Default, merge_layers, fill_capture_gaps, keyword normalization, rating sanitizing, and the temporary read_supplemental_metadata stub.
Create empty-but-valid iptc.rs, xmp.rs, packets.rs, and sidecar.rs modules and declare them from mod.rs.

Add unit tests whose names start with file_metadata_merge_ and file_metadata_gaps_. Cover first-non-empty wins, empty string does not override, keyword order and caps, rating -1 and 6 rejected, rating 0 kept, and capture fill that does not replace an existing make or invent orientation.

title: Parse IPTC IIM datasets into FileMetadata
description: Implement a byte-level IPTC IIM reader. JPEG APP13 and TIFF tag 33723 store this block. The container task will locate the bytes; this task only parses an IIM payload into FileMetadata. Lap has no IPTC reader today.
acceptance_criteria: The parser reads dataset 1:90 and datasets 2:05, 2:25, 2:55, 2:60, 2:80, 2:90, 2:95, 2:101, 2:105, 2:110, 2:116, and 2:120 into title, keywords, capture date, creator, city, state, country, headline, credit, copyright, and description.
UTF-8 is used when 1:90 is the IPTC UTF-8 designation ESC % G. Otherwise bytes are decoded as Latin-1. Repeated 2:25 datasets become multiple keywords.
A truncated dataset, an unknown dataset, or an invalid date skips that dataset and still returns the fields that parsed. The function does not panic and does not return an error for malformed input.

Date Created is formatted as YYYY:MM:DD HH:MM:SS when Time Created is present, or YYYY:MM:DD 00:00:00 when only the date is present, so the existing meta_date_to_timestamp helper can parse it later. IPTC urgency is not converted into a rating.
constraints: Accept a payload that is either a raw IIM byte string or an IIM byte string wrapped in a Photoshop 8BIM resource. Do not require a full JPEG.
Do not read the filesystem and do not modify FileMetadata merge rules.
implementation_notes: Public entry point: parse_iptc(payload: &[u8]) -> FileMetadata in iptc.rs.

IIM records start with 0x1C, then record number, dataset number, and a big-endian length. When the high bit of the length is set, the lower 15 bits are the number of following length bytes. Cap one dataset at 64 KiB and the whole payload at 2 MiB.
If the payload begins with the 8BIM signature, scan Photoshop image resources and parse resource id 0x0404 as the IIM payload. Ignore other resource ids.
Tests should build byte fixtures in memory. Include one UTF-8 keyword fixture and one Latin-1 fixture with a non-ASCII byte.
implementation_steps: Implement the IIM record walker and the 8BIM 0x0404 unwrapper in iptc.rs.
Map the datasets listed in the acceptance criteria onto FileMetadata. Leave capture exposure, GPS, camera, lens, label, and rating empty.
Decode text using the coded character set seen so far in the block. If 1:90 appears after text datasets, Latin-1 remains the default for datasets that preceded it.

Add file_metadata_iptc_ tests for a multi-keyword block, a headline plus caption, a CCYYMMDD date with and without time, a truncated final record, and an 8BIM wrapper whose only metadata resource is 0x0404.

title: Parse XMP packets into FileMetadata
description: Implement an XMP reader for the descriptive and capture fields Lap can index. The same parser must work for an embedded packet and for a sidecar file body. Lap currently scans XMP only to find a motion-photo video offset, which must be left unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: parse_xmp reads dc:title, dc:description, dc:subject, dc:creator, dc:rights, photoshop:Headline, photoshop:Credit, photoshop:DateCreated, photoshop:City, photoshop:State, photoshop:Country, xmp:CreateDate, xmp:Rating, xmp:Label, exif:DateTimeOriginal, exif GPS latitude, longitude, altitude and their refs, tiff:Make, tiff:Model, tiff:Artist, tiff:Copyright, tiff:ImageDescription, and aux or crs lens make and model.
rdf:Alt, rdf:Bag, and rdf:Seq values are collected. Language alternatives use the x-default item when present, otherwise the first item. Keywords preserve bag order.

GPS accepts decimal degrees and EXIF-style degrees,minutes,seconds with a N, S, E, or W ref. Out-of-range coordinates are ignored. Timezone-less dates become YYYY:MM:DD HH:MM:SS local text. Dates with an explicit offset are left as RFC3339 text that meta_date_to_timestamp already accepts.

xmp:Rating outside 0 through 5 is discarded. crs develop settings other than lens identity are ignored. External XML entities are not resolved. A packet larger than 2 MiB yields an empty FileMetadata. Malformed XML yields an empty FileMetadata and does not panic.
constraints: Do not change t_motion_photo.rs.
Do not enable XML features that fetch remote DTDs or entities.
Keep the new dependency limited to XMP parsing.
implementation_notes: Add the quick-xml crate to src-tauri/Cargo.toml. Pin a current 0.x compatible release and do not enable unneeded features.
Public entry point: parse_xmp(xml: &str) -> FileMetadata. Strip the UTF-8 BOM and ignore an xpacket wrapper around x:xmpmeta.
Match elements by local name and by the namespace URI suffix or prefix used by Adobe packets: dc, photoshop, xmp, exif, tiff, aux, and crs. Accept both prefixed names and default xmlns declarations.
Prefer exif:DateTimeOriginal over photoshop:DateCreated over xmp:CreateDate. Do not read xmp:ModifyDate or xmp:MetadataDate into capture_date.
Tests are in-memory XML strings. Include a bag of subjects, an Alt with x-default, a decimal GPS pair, a DMS GPS pair, rating -1, and a deliberately truncated packet.
implementation_steps: Add quick-xml to the Tauri crate dependencies.
Implement a streaming or tree walk that collects the accepted properties and RDF list items into FileMetadata.
Implement GPS and date normalization helpers next to the parser.
Add file_metadata_xmp_ tests for the acceptance fixtures, plus a packet that contains only crs tone settings and asserts the result is empty apart from any lens fields.

title: Extract IPTC and XMP packets from image containers
description: Locate raw IPTC and XMP payloads inside the image formats Lap already indexes. This does not interpret the payloads and does not replace read_exif_permissive, little_exif, or LibRaw. JPEG segment walking already exists in t_image.rs; follow that style and keep the new walker inside the metadata module so indexing can call one function.
acceptance_criteria: extract_packets(path) returns the raw IPTC payload and the raw XMP XML string when those packets exist. Missing packets are empty options. IO errors and unrecognized containers return empty packets rather than an error.

JPEG APP1 segments whose header is http://ns.adobe.com/xap/1.0/ yield XMP. JPEG APP13 segments yield the 8BIM resource 0x0404 payload, or the raw APP13 body when the parser task will unwrap 8BIM. EXIF APP1 segments are not returned as XMP.
PNG returns XML from iTXt, zTXt, or tEXt chunks named XML:com.adobe.xmp. TIFF-family files, including TIFF-based RAW, return IFD tag 700 as XMP and tag 33723 as IPTC. WebP returns the XMP RIFF chunk.

HEIC, AVIF, and other containers that are not parsed structurally are scanned only in the first 8 MiB for an x:xmpmeta or xpacket block. The scan does not load the rest of a large RAW or video-sized file. A packet over 2 MiB is discarded.
constraints: Do not decode pixels and do not call LibRaw.
Stop a JPEG walk at the start of scan, or at the entropy-coded data, so the compressed image is not read.
Tests must build temporary files from byte fixtures and delete them. Do not commit binary sample photos.
implementation_notes: Public entry point: extract_packets(path: &Path) -> MetadataPackets { iptc: Option<Vec<u8>>, xmp: Option<String> }.

For TIFF, a minimal IFD reader is enough: endianness from II or MM, one IFD, inline and offset values for tags 700 and 33723. If the TIFF is malformed, return empty packets. Do not try to be a general TIFF parser.
Inflate PNG zTXt with the flate2 crate already in Cargo.toml. Cap the inflated output at 2 MiB.
The bounded text scan is only the fallback after the container-specific readers decline the file. It must reject a match that has no closing x:xmpmeta or xpacket end within the cap.
implementation_steps: Implement JPEG APP1 XMP and APP13 collection by walking markers.
Implement PNG chunk collection and TIFF tag 700 and 33723 collection.
Implement the WebP XMP chunk reader and the 8 MiB bounded XMP fallback.

Add file_metadata_packets_ tests: a minimal JPEG with one XMP APP1 and one APP13, a JPEG whose only APP1 is EXIF, a PNG iTXt packet, a little-endian TIFF with tag 700, a file larger than 8 MiB whose only XMP is past the cap, and an unreadable path.

title: Discover the XMP sidecar bound to an image
description: Find the single XMP sidecar that belongs to a media file and return its text and a change stamp. Lap already ignores .xmp during scans so those files are not indexed as photos. This task defines which sidecar is bound to which image. It does not parse the XML and does not move files.
acceptance_criteria: An exact sidecar named <file name>.xmp, compared case-insensitively, binds only to that file. Example: IMG.JPG.xmp binds to IMG.JPG and not to IMG.CR2.

A stem sidecar named <stem>.xmp binds to the only media sibling with that stem. When several media siblings share the stem, it binds only to the RAW file. A non-RAW sibling in that group does not use the stem sidecar.

bound_sidecar never returns a path outside the image directory, never returns an .aae file, and ignores directories and files larger than 2 MiB. sidecar_stamp is None when no sidecar is bound. Otherwise it is a stable string containing the sidecar path, mtime in seconds, and length.
read_sidecar_xml returns the file text only after the size check. Missing, unreadable, or oversized sidecars return None. Discovery does not create, rename, or delete anything.
constraints: Use the same media extensions as get_file_type in t_utils.rs: NORMAL_IMGS, FFMPEG_BACKED_IMGS, and RAW_IMGS. Do not treat .xmp or .aae as media.
Do not import the XMP parser here. Return text only.
Keep .xmp files excluded from library scanning. Do not remove them from is_ignored_scan_sidecar.
implementation_notes: Public functions: bound_sidecar(media_path: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf>, read_sidecar_xml(media_path: &Path) -> Option<String>, and sidecar_stamp(media_path: &Path) -> Option<String>.
On case-insensitive filesystems, opening the exact name the user has is enough. When listing the directory for the ambiguous stem rule, compare stems case-insensitively.
Prefer the exact sidecar over the stem sidecar when both exist.
Stamp format: lowercase absolute path, mtime seconds, and length, separated by |. Tests can assert that changing the length changes the stamp and that deleting the file makes the stamp None.
File operations will call bound_sidecar later. Keep the binding rules in this module so rename and index cannot drift.
implementation_steps: Implement exact and stem candidate names and the RAW-only rule for shared stems.
Implement the size, directory, and extension guards.
Implement stamp and XML read using those guards.

Add file_metadata_sidecar_ tests in a temporary directory: exact sidecar wins, shared stem binds only to the RAW sibling, a lone JPEG uses the stem sidecar, an .aae sibling is ignored, and a sidecar over 2 MiB is ignored.

title: Persist supplemental metadata on catalog rows
description: Add nullable file-owned columns for the descriptive values EXIF columns do not cover, plus a backfill version and a sidecar stamp. Existing afiles rows are migrated idempotently. This task stores and loads the columns. It does not parse images.
acceptance_criteria: afiles gains e_title, e_headline, e_keywords, e_credit, e_label, e_location, embedded_rating, embedded_metadata_version, and metadata_sidecar_stamp. e_keywords is a JSON array of strings. embedded_rating is NULL when the file has no rating. embedded_metadata_version is NULL until a reader fills it.
Fresh databases and databases already at user_version 17 both end with these columns. Running the migration twice does not fail. user_version becomes 18.

AFile insert, update, build_base_query, and from_row round-trip the new fields. The positional select in t_dedup.rs stays aligned with from_row. Serialized file JSON uses the existing snake_case names, including embedded_rating and e_keywords as an array.

AFile::update continues to write the Lap rating column from the struct and does not treat embedded_rating as that column. Library columns is_favorite, comments, culling_flag, rotate, and has_tags stay on their current write paths.
constraints: Append new select expressions at the end of the AFile select list, immediately before FROM, and append matching from_row indexes. Do not insert columns into the middle of the positional list.
Follow the guarded ALTER style used by migration 16. Also add the columns to the fresh CREATE TABLE for afiles so new and migrated databases match.
Do not change search SQL in this task.
implementation_notes: Current highest migration version is 17. Add version 18 with an empty sql string and a match arm that calls a focused helper, following migrate_tag_groups.
Store keywords as JSON text in SQLite and as Vec<String> on AFile. Invalid JSON loads as an empty vector. Build e_location later; this task only persists the string.
Update every insert and update parameter list and the duplicated select in t_dedup.rs. Search the repository for a.e_orientation and motion_photo_offset selects before finishing.
The in-memory tag-group query test builds a tiny afiles table and only runs search SQL when searchFileName is empty. Do not make the base select mandatory for that test.
implementation_steps: Add the nine columns to the CREATE TABLE statement and to migration 18 using table_has_column guards.
Add the fields to AFile, Default construction in new_with_raw_info, insert, update, build_base_query, and from_row.
Update the dedup select and its row.get indexes by the same appended positions.
Add a file_metadata_schema_ test that creates an afiles table missing the new columns, runs the version 18 helper, checks the columns exist, and runs the helper again successfully.

title: Fill indexed metadata from IPTC, XMP, and sidecars
description: During image and RAW indexing, combine the existing EXIF and LibRaw results with embedded IPTC, embedded XMP, and the bound sidecar. Descriptive values follow sidecar-over-embedded precedence. Capture values already found by the current readers stay authoritative. Video files keep the current t_video path.
acceptance_criteria: read_supplemental_metadata reads packets and the bound sidecar, parses them, and merges layers in this order: exact-or-stem sidecar XMP, embedded XMP, embedded IPTC. A failure in any layer leaves the other layers intact and still returns a FileMetadata.

For file types 1 and 3, empty e_artist, e_copyright, e_description, camera, lens, exposure, ISO, flash, and software fields are filled from the supplemental value. taken_date is replaced only when the current value is still the file mtime fallback. GPS is filled only when latitude and longitude are both missing, and geocoding then uses the existing local geocoder.

e_title, e_headline, e_keywords, e_credit, e_label, e_location, and embedded_rating are set from the merged descriptive metadata. e_location joins non-empty city, state, and country with commas. embedded_metadata_version is set to 1 and metadata_sidecar_stamp is the stamp from the sidecar module.

e_orientation, width, height, media_subtype, motion_photo_offset, and content_identifier are unchanged by the supplemental merge. Lap rating, favorites, comments, tags, and culling are not taken from the file. PNG AI comment extraction into the comments column is unchanged.
A JPEG whose EXIF already contains artist and exposure keeps those EXIF values even when the sidecar contains different ones. The sidecar still supplies keywords and title.
constraints: Do not call the supplemental reader for videos.
Do not delete thumbnails, clear embeds, or rewrite sidecars from this path.
Factor extraction so the refresh task can reuse it without a second copy of the precedence rules.
If supplemental reading panics or returns no data, indexing continues with today's EXIF behavior.
implementation_notes: Replace the stub read_supplemental_metadata. It should call extract_packets, parse_iptc, parse_xmp, read_sidecar_xml, and merge_layers. Catch parser failures per layer.
Apply the result near the end of the image and RAW branch in AFile::new_with_raw_info, after EXIF, little_exif, LibRaw, and the binary scrape. Use fill_capture_gaps against the fields already chosen.
Extract a helper used by new_with_raw_info, for example apply_supplemental_metadata(&mut fields, path, file_type), so a later refresh can apply the same helper onto an existing row.
Keep update_file_info copying the previous Lap rating onto the new struct before AFile::update. Put embedded_rating on the new struct from the file, not from the old Lap rating.
Do not log the parsed values. A short debug line that names the file and says supplemental metadata was skipped is enough on failure.
implementation_steps: Implement read_supplemental_metadata with the three-layer merge and per-layer isolation.
Add apply_supplemental_metadata and call it from the image and RAW branch of new_with_raw_info after existing readers and before the AFile struct is built.
Populate the new columns, version 1, and sidecar stamp in that struct so insert and the mtime-based update persist them.

Add file_metadata_index_ tests using temporary JPEG or raw packet fixtures: sidecar keywords override embedded keywords, existing EXIF artist is kept, missing GPS is filled from XMP, orientation in XMP is ignored, and a broken sidecar still keeps embedded IPTC.

title: Refresh metadata when a sidecar changes and backfill older rows
description: Album scan currently skips files whose image mtime is unchanged. Sidecar edits do not change that mtime, and rows indexed before this feature have a null embedded_metadata_version. Re-read file metadata in those cases without the destructive path used for a modified image.
acceptance_criteria: On an otherwise unchanged image or RAW file, scan re-reads supplemental metadata when embedded_metadata_version is null or below 1, or when sidecar_stamp differs from the stored metadata_sidecar_stamp, including when the sidecar disappeared and the stamp became empty.

The refresh updates file-derived metadata columns, taken_date, GPS, geo columns, the supplemental columns, the version, and the stamp. It does not change width, height, duration, thumbnails, embeds, media_subtype, motion_photo_offset, content_identifier, is_favorite, rating, comments, culling_flag, rotate, tags, or collections.
A normal mtime change still uses the existing update_file_info path, including thumbnail and embedding invalidation. A sidecar-only refresh does not.
After the sidecar is removed, fields that came only from the sidecar are cleared or replaced by embedded IPTC or XMP, and EXIF values remain. The sidecar file itself is not modified.
constraints: Do not point tests at the user's real Lap database. open_conn is the process library connection.
Reuse apply_supplemental_metadata and the existing EXIF extraction helper rather than copying precedence rules.
Backfill may re-read each image once. It must not regenerate thumbnails or embeddings.
implementation_notes: In add_to_db_with_raw_info, after the existing early returns, detect a metadata-only refresh before the final last_scan_time touch. The motion-photo one-time path must still run when it applies.
Prefer a narrow UPDATE for the metadata columns, modeled on refresh_motion_photo_detection, so a full AFile::update cannot clobber rating. Copy nothing from XMP into rating.
Recompute geo_name and the admin fields only when the refreshed GPS pair changed. Use the existing local geocoder. Clear geo fields when GPS is cleared.
Store version constant 1 in one place shared with the indexer.
implementation_steps: Add a predicate for null or stale embedded_metadata_version and for a changed sidecar stamp. Stat the sidecar only; do not parse when the stamp matches and the version is current.
Implement refresh_embedded_metadata that reuses the index helper and writes the narrow column set, then marks last_scan_time.
Call it from the unchanged-file branch and return status 2 so the scan counts the file as updated.

Add file_metadata_refresh_ tests: a stale version schedules a refresh; a matching stamp does not parse; rating and an embeds blob survive the SQL the refresh runs; removing a sidecar clears a sidecar-only title while keeping an EXIF artist.

title: Keep bound XMP sidecars with Lap file operations
description: If Lap renames, moves, copies, imports, or deletes an image and leaves its XMP sidecar behind, the next scan will lose or mis-attach the metadata it just learned to read. Extend the existing sidecar transfer behavior so the bound XMP file follows the image. Do not parse or rewrite sidecar contents. AAE handling stays as it is.
acceptance_criteria: Rename, move, copy, date-organized import, and delete use bound_sidecar from the metadata module. The destination sidecar name is derived from the destination image name, including a conflict suffix. An exact sidecar stays exact, and a stem sidecar stays a stem sidecar.

A RAW-plus-JPEG pair that shares one stem sidecar transfers that sidecar once, with the RAW file. The JPEG transfer does not move or delete that same sidecar again. Distinct exact sidecars follow their own files.
Delete and trash remove or trash the bound sidecar with the image. A failed sidecar transfer rolls back with the same pattern already used for AAE sidecars. The operation does not modify XML.
AAE files are still transferred by the Apple sidecar helpers and are not selected as XMP. .xmp files remain ignored by the media scan.
constraints: Do not duplicate the exact-versus-stem binding rules. Call bound_sidecar.
Do not write metadata into the sidecar while renaming it.
Keep is_ignored_scan_sidecar covering xmp and aae.
implementation_notes: Follow the call sites that already plan AAE transfers: build_apple_sidecar_rename_plan, the import copy path in t_utils.rs, and delete_apple_aae_sidecars in t_cmds.rs. A parallel XMP plan is appropriate if folding XMP into the AAE structs makes those structs misleading.
Deduplicate source paths the way seen_sidecar_paths already does, so one shared stem sidecar is not renamed twice.
When the destination sidecar path already exists, fail that transfer with the existing conflict style instead of overwriting an unrelated XMP file.
Tests can use a temporary directory and the pure path planner. They do not need a catalog database.
implementation_steps: Add an XMP transfer plan that asks bound_sidecar for the source and builds the destination name from the destination media file.
Invoke that plan from rename, move, copy, import, and delete next to the AAE calls. Roll back renamed sidecars if a later step fails.
Deduplicate shared stem sidecars inside a grouped RAW-plus-JPEG operation.

Add file_metadata_transfer_ tests: exact sidecar rename, stem sidecar follows a conflict-suffixed RAW name once, JPEG in the pair does not take it, an existing destination sidecar is a conflict, and an .aae file is not returned by the XMP plan.

title: Show supplemental metadata in the file info panel
